items.t: Gukbap — rice already in the soup
items.d: The default almost everywhere else in Korea. One bowl, rice spooned in back in the kitchen.

items.t: Ttarogukbap — rice in its own bowl
items.d: 'Ttaro' means 'separately'. You decide how much rice goes in, and when — or whether it goes in at all.
Beef bone broth simmered over ten hours, heavy on green onion and radish, with seonji (blood curd) in the bowl.

slides.title:
A dish named
after a request
slides.body:
Gugil opened in 1946 as a market stall run by Seo Dong-sul and Kim Yi-soon. At the start the rice came already spooned into the broth, the way gukbap is served anywhere else.

The Encyclopedia of Daegu Culture records that after the Korean War some customers began asking for the rice and the soup to arrive separately, and that obliging them became the house standard. The dish's name is literally that request.

What this shop is credited with is not a recipe but a way of serving one — and Daegu is now the city where the two bowls come apart by default.

items.t: Open 24 hours, closed one day at the major holidays
items.d: Per the Daegu city listing as of September 2026. A call to 053-253-7623 is worth it before a late-night detour
Special ttarogukbap 12,000 won, ttaroguksu (the noodle version) 11,000 won. Around 150 seats, and the lunch rush fills them
